ns2:course.label: Cultural Psychology
ns2:course.description: Explores cultural influences on attitudes, cognition, and behavior. The focus is social psychological but the readings draw on work across several fields, both inside psychology and outside psychology. Subjects have included cultural influences on violence, analytic vs. holistic thinking styles, economic behavior, parenting and education, and the construction of self. Methodological issues in making cross-cultural comparisons will be discussed. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit.
